exposure: transcatheter arterial embolization (TAE) of the inferior mesenteric artery (IMA)
Transcatheter arterial embolization (TAE) of the inferior mesenteric artery (IMA)
outcome: Safety and efficacy of TAE of the IMA for postpartum hemorrhage (PPH)
cohort: 8 patients (mean age 34.4 years) who underwent TAE of the IMA for PPH between March 2001 and September 2018
finding: This retrospective analysis suggests that TAE of the IMA is a safe and effective treatment option for postpartum hemorrhage, particularly in cases of persistent vaginal bleeding after embolization of the bilateral iliac arteries.
mod_finding: TAE of the IMA was successful in stopping bleeding in all 8 patients who had PPH after vaginal delivery, with no reported complications or bowel ischemia during follow-up.
